title: Verification rewrites or retires a desired behavior only to follow merged code
answers: can verify change a behavior note
what happens when the code behind a behavior changes
body: A `behavior` note is a rule a person wrote. When its deps change, src/ops.js:verifyNote hands it to src/ops.js:verifyBehavior, whose verdicts are `holds` (re-baseline), `moved` (deps re-pointed, history kept), and for code that no longer upholds it either `broken` or `revised`, decided by src/ops.js:onDefaultBranch: code that is not merged (a working tree, a branch, unpushed commits) leaves the text alone and sets status `violated` with the commit and reason; code merged on the default branch is the truth, and the behavior's body is replaced with what the code upholds now, the old body kept in `history` and `revised` recording the commit and reason. One path retires a behavior, and only for merged code: when every file it rested on is gone from the default branch, src/ops.js:refresh retires it with no model call (src/ops.js:anchorsGone), and a revision that would leave it with no dep at all is the verdict `retired` instead of a fresh behavior with nothing to rest on; the text and the deps go to `history`, and the person is named it at the end of the next turn. Nothing lowers a behavior's confidence or rewrites it for unmerged code; the ordinary verdicts `update` and `invalid` never reach a behavior.

history.reason: revised by hand on 2026-10-04: merged code is the truth, so a behavior follows it
history.prevBody: A `behavior` note is a rule a person wrote; when its deps change, verification asks whether the code still upholds it, never whether the note is right. src/ops.js:verifyNote hands every behavior to src/ops.js:verifyBehavior, whose verdicts are `holds` (re-baseline), `broken` (status `violated`, with the commit and reason; the text is left alone) and `moved` (deps re-pointed, history kept). No path sets a behavior to `invalid`, replaces its body, or lowers its confidence. The ordinary note verdicts `update` and `invalid` must never reach a behavior.
